newsitem.title: KENYA: Foreign demand nudges Kenyan bourse index higher.
newsitem.headline: Foreign demand nudges Kenyan bourse index higher.

text.p: Increased demand from foreign investors for selected blue chip shares on Wednesday pushed the Nairobi Stock Exchange 20-share index 5.70 points higher to 3472.03 points, bourse officials said.
Turnover was posted at 21.454 million shillings on 525,207 shares, compared to 32.159 million shillings on 540,610 shares on Tuesday.
Foreigners bought Firestone East Africa at between 30-33 from 28.25, Kenya Commercial Bank at 90 unchanged and Uchumi at 37.50 from 36.75.
"This heavy interest from foreign investors is likely to continue for the better part of the year as they are capitalising on low prices expected to prevail," a senior broker said.
He said prices were undervalued because of caution on the part of investors in the run-up to general elections which are supposed to be called within the next year.
Brokers said that in the near term prices could rise higher with market expectations riding high on positive year-end results, especially among the financials.
Barclays Bank closed at 116 from 115 while Kenya Power & Lighting gained eight to close at 115. Standard Chartered Bank closed at 56 from 55.50 while Kenya Airways traded at 8.70 from 8.60.
British American Tobacco (BAT) announced a final dividend of four shillings per share. It recorded a profit of 1,005 million shillings before tax compared to 824 million last year.
The NSE daily report said the plantations accounted for only two percent of the day's trading.
Brokers said this was due to pessimism over a poor crop expected this year as a result of drought.
Rea Vipingo traded at 11.25 from 11 while Sasini Tea & Coffee was unchanged at 60. Brooke Bond was unchanged at 150.
The East African Development corporate bond traded some 11 million shillings at 99.99 percent from 99.70 on February 5.
